in_text_mentions: The perilobular pattern is characterized by curved or arcade-like bands of parenchymal consolidation with blurred borders and thickening of the interlobular septa—resembling a Roman Arch (Figure 6) [22]. It is a perilobular pattern and often associated with other opacities, especially consolidations [17,24]. The presence of air bronchogram sign helps to differentiate this pattern from atelectasis and fibrotic bands; other conditions that must be excluded are post-primary tuberculosis, lymphomatoid granulomatosis, lymphangitic carcinomatosis, fungal infections, sarcoidosis, pulmonary infarction
